title: The SKY Backstop is currently limitless even though the Atlas requires an emission rate and a per-event maximum to be defined
content:
Four provisions in A.3.6 sit in unresolved tension.

A.3.6.1 requires that "an emissions rate for the SKY backstop function that prevents risk of sudden failure must be defined," A.3.6.2 requires that "a maximum level of SKY emission per undercollateralization event must be defined," and A.3.6.4 requires a halt mechanism that "immediately halts the backstop event in case of severe risk of total failure." All three are stated as requirements in the future tense, with no values or contracts specified.

A.3.6.1.1 then records the present state in one line: "The SKY Backstop is temporarily limitless."

The gap matters because other provisions already depend on the missing pieces. A.3.6.5 governs what happens "in case the backstop limit is reached and not overridden, or in case the backstop is halted" — but with no limit and no halt mechanism, that branch is currently unreachable and the peg-haircut path it defines is dormant. A.3.6.3's override mechanism, which exists to permit emission *beyond* the maximum, is likewise moot while there is no maximum.

So the Atlas is transparent about an unimplemented safeguard rather than concealing it, and the word "temporarily" flags the intent. But the live behaviour today is unbounded dilution during a Backstop Event, with the reflexive risk A.3.6.1 was written to prevent left unmitigated. This is a section to re-check against any later revision of the Stability Scope.
description: A.3.6.1.1 declares it 'temporarily limitless' while A.3.6.1, A.3.6.2 and A.3.6.4 state only that a rate, a maximum and a halt mechanism must be defined — the safeguards are unwritten.
